distinctive-massing.evidence: More developed portal, screens, clerestory and roof profile, but familiar mirrored-wing composition with unresolved junctions does not establish exceptional coherent luxury architecture.

volume-hierarchy.evidence: Central hall span and rising roof imply hierarchy; near-equal roof heights and intersecting roof junctions remain unresolved.

six-individual-suites.evidence: Six dedicated doors and explicit partitions improve specificity; ground doors miss openings by 4 m and wall loops remain unclosed. All suites remain allocated capacity.

circulation-and-arrival.evidence: Solid stair reserve blocks principal doorway; arrival and terrace links have 3 m/2 m gaps. Upper slab strips can support potential side corridors but full access is unresolved.

waterfront-and-outdoor-relationships.evidence: Hollow coping/basin and supported shade improve the proposal; hall-to-terrace gap, schematic landscape and absent infinity edge remain.

construction-precision.evidence: Six spatial-intent mismatches, nine space-bound mismatches, invalid anchor/kind references, incomplete wall loops, blocking stair volume and intersecting roof junctions prevent faithful complete construction.

estate-ambition.evidence: More substantial component development and a ceremonial sequence; added area does not resolve service organization, suite independence, circulation or complete landscape composition.

conclusion: Sol is better developed than Terra but fails the architectural goal. Preserve as rejected evidence; no construction and no production model switch justified by this single pair.
method: Manual coordinate-based review with same existing seven criteria; no provider review, render or geometry repair.
